rest.seal.answers.unreadable: Any endpoint, when the body cannot be parsed as JSON. Checked before the token.
rest.seal.answers.tokenRefused: An endpoint that takes a token, when seal's own check refuses it: no `Authorization: Bearer` header, a signature identity's published keys do not verify, another issuer or audience, an expired token, or a token that is not an access token. Refresh the access token or sign in again.
rest.seal.answers.tooLarge: Any endpoint that takes a body, when the body is larger than the endpoint allows: 1 KiB for a credential request, 2 KiB for an approval, 16 KiB for a presentation.
rest.seal.answers.notJson: Any endpoint that takes a body, when its `Content-Type` is not one seal reads, such as a form.
rest.seal.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when seal fails in a way it did not expect, its database being unreachable included. `traceId` names the request in seal's log.
rest.seal.answers.identityUnavailable: An endpoint that takes a token, when seal cannot read identity's published keys to check it. Nothing was decided; try again shortly.
rest.seal.listPredicates.summary: List the predicates an admin has approved, each with the rows seal keeps in the credential registry.
rest.seal.listPredicates.who: Anyone, without a token: holders and verifiers read the same list.
rest.seal.listPredicates.case.listed: Always, with the active registry's generation and address (`registry` is `null` while none is active). Only live predicates are listed. Each row's `id` is the contract's id for those four minimums, `placed` says whether the registry holds it yet, and `current` marks this period's row.
rest.seal.getPredicate.summary: Read one predicate, withdrawn or live.
rest.seal.getPredicate.field.id: The predicate's `id` from the list or from an approval, a UUID in lower case.
rest.seal.getPredicate.case.found: When the predicate exists. A withdrawn one has `status` `withdrawn`, its `withdrawnAt`, and no rows.
rest.seal.getPredicate.case.notFound: When no predicate has this `id`, or the `id` is not a UUID in lower case.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.summary: Approve a predicate: the minimums a credential must meet, and how recent it must be.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.who: An admin, from the staff network. Seal checks the token's role itself; identity issues an admin's token only after the second factor.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.field.label: The name holders and verifiers see, 1 to 80 printable characters; sent trimmed.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.field.minimum: Exactly the class's three minimums, whole numbers: for couriers `deliveries` (0 to 1,000,000), `ratingHundredths` (0 to 500, a rating of 4.50 is `450`) and `daysActive` (0 to 36,525). The fourth attribute, the issue day, is derived from `freshnessDays`.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.field.freshne: How recent a credential must be, in days, 1 to 365. Each week's row asks for an issue day on or after that week's first day less this window.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.case.approved: When the caller is an admin and no live predicate has the same minimums and window. The rows are not placed yet: seal writes them to the registry within about ten minutes.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.case.invalid: When the body is not exactly these four fields within the class's bounds.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.case.notAdmin: When the token is valid but not an admin's.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.case.exists: When a live predicate of the class already has these minimums and this window.
rest.seal.approvePredicate.case.full: When the class already has eight live predicates. Withdraw one first.
rest.seal.withdrawPredicate.summary: Withdraw a predicate, so no new presentation is made under its rows.
rest.seal.withdrawPredicate.who: An admin, from the staff network.
rest.seal.withdrawPredicate.field.id: The predicate's `id`, a UUID in lower case.
rest.seal.withdrawPredicate.case.withdra: When the predicate is withdrawn, and again for one already withdrawn. Seal takes its rows out of the registry within about ten minutes; what was proven under them stays readable.
rest.seal.withdrawPredicate.case.notAdmi: When the token is valid but not an admin's.
rest.seal.withdrawPredicate.case.notFoun: When no predicate has this `id`, or the `id` is not a UUID in lower case.
rest.seal.requestCourierCredential.summa: Ask for a credential of the courier's own record, bound to a key only the courier's phone holds.
rest.seal.requestCourierCredential.who: A courier, with their own access token. Kong checks the token first, and seal checks it again together with the role.
rest.seal.requestCourierCredential.field: The holder's public key, which the holder runtime computes from the secret the phone keeps: a field element written in decimal, with no leading zero. The body is exactly this one field.
When the courier already has today's credential under this same key. The answer is that credential as it stands now, as in step 4.

When seal records a new credential. `attributes` are the courier's deliveries, rating in hundredths, days active and the issue day, counted in days since 1970-01-01 UTC. It stays `pending` until seal has written it to the registry, usually within a few minutes; read it at `Location` until it is `issued`.
When the body is not exactly `{ holderPublicKey }` holding a field element in decimal.
When the token is valid but its role is not `courier`, such as a token from before an admin approved the courier.
When the courier has not delivered an order yet.
When the courier already has today's credential under another key, for example after reinstalling the app. A courier gets one credential a day, the day counted in UTC: ask again tomorrow.
When seal's copies of matching's deliveries and review's ratings are more than five minutes behind. Nothing was recorded; try again after `Retry-After`.
rest.seal.getCourierCredential.summary: Read one of the courier's credentials, to see whether the registry holds it yet.
rest.seal.getCourierCredential.who: The courier it was issued to, with their own access token; anyone else gets `404`.
rest.seal.getCourierCredential.field.id: The credential's `id` from step 3, a UUID in lower case.
rest.seal.getCourierCredential.case.foun: When the credential is the caller's. `status` is `pending` until the active registry holds it, and `issued` once it does, with `registry` saying where: `leafIndex` is what the holder proves against. It is `superseded` when the active registry does not hold it and a newer credential of the courier's has taken its place, since after a new registry generation seal writes only each courier's latest credential again.
rest.seal.getCourierCredential.case.notF: When the caller has no credential with this `id`, or the `id` is not a UUID in lower case.
rest.seal.holder.summary: Find the holder runtime, the page that makes the courier's proofs on the phone.
rest.seal.holder.case.found: Always. `digest` names the build, a SHA-256 over its files; `entry` is the page to load, and `notices` lists the licences of what it bundles. The answer changes only with a seal release.
rest.seal.holderFile.summary: Load a file of the holder runtime: its page, script, WebAssembly, proving keys and notices.
rest.seal.holderFile.field.file: A file of that build. A client loads `index.html`, which loads the rest itself.
rest.seal.holderFile.case.page: For `index.html`. The policy lets the page run only its own script and WebAssembly and talk only to the API host.
rest.seal.holderFile.case.file: For any other file of the build, typed by its name: `text/javascript`, `application/wasm`, `text/plain`, or `application/octet-stream` for the proving keys and parameters. A build never changes, so a client may keep its files for a year.
rest.seal.holderFile.case.notFound: When the digest is not the build seal serves now, or the build has no such file. A client holding an old `entry` reads step 1 again.
rest.seal.registrySnapshot.summary: Read the credential registry's public state, which the holder proves against without asking seal again.
rest.seal.registrySnapshot.case.read: When the active registry could be read, at most a minute ago. `contractState`, `zswapChainState` and `ledgerParameters` are the chain's state, serialized and in hex, tens of kilobytes together; `networkId` is the Midnight network they come from.
rest.seal.registrySnapshot.case.unavaila: When no registry is active, or the chain's indexer cannot be read. A client keeps the snapshot it has and tries again after `Retry-After`.
rest.seal.relayPresentation.summary: Hand a holder's presentation to seal, which pays its fee and sends it to the chain.
rest.seal.relayPresentation.who: Anyone, without a token: usually the verifier the courier's phone gave the answer to. Kong allows 20 a minute from one address on this route.
rest.seal.relayPresentation.field.transa: The proven, bound transaction the holder made, in lowercase hex, about 3.6 KB as bytes. It carries the proof, the challenge and the row's `id`, and none of the courier's numbers. The body is exactly this one field.
rest.seal.relayPresentation.case.relayed: When the transaction is a single call to the active registry's `present` and seal's sponsor wallet has paid for it and sent it. `txId` names it on Midnight. The challenge counts as answered once the chain includes it, usually within a minute: read step 7.
rest.seal.relayPresentation.case.invalid: When the body is not exactly `{ transaction }` holding whole bytes in lowercase hex.
rest.seal.relayPresentation.case.notPres: When the bytes are not a proven, bound transaction, or the transaction moves coins, makes more than one call, or calls anything but the active registry's `present`. `message` says which.
rest.seal.relayPresentation.case.noRegis: When no registry generation is active, as after a Midnight network reset until seal has deployed the next one.
rest.seal.relayPresentation.case.sponsor: When seal's sponsor wallet cannot pay now, for example while it syncs. Nothing was sent. The transaction stays valid for an hour after the holder made it: try again after `Retry-After`.
rest.seal.presentationStatus.summary: Read whether a challenge has been answered, and under which row.
rest.seal.presentationStatus.field.chall: The challenge the verifier put in its request, 32 bytes in lowercase hex.
rest.seal.presentationStatus.case.answer: When a presentation of this challenge is on chain, read at most five seconds ago. `predicateId` is the row the proof met; a verifier accepts the answer only when it is the row the verifier asked for.
rest.seal.presentationStatus.case.unansw: When the active registry holds no presentation of this challenge yet.
rest.seal.presentationStatus.case.invali: When the challenge is not 64 lowercase hex characters.
rest.seal.presentationStatus.case.unavai: When no registry is active, or the chain cannot be read. Try again after `Retry-After`.
